mainTopic: רבן גמליאל's authority over קידוש החודש, the clash with רבי יהושע, and why every בית דין carries the authority of משה's court
overview: The משנה tells of two cases where רבן גמליאל accepted witnesses about the new moon even though other חכמים called them עדי שקר. When רבי יהושע sided with רבי דוסא בן הורכינס against him, רבן גמליאל ordered רבי יהושע to come with his staff and money on the day רבי יהושע counted as יום הכפורים. רבי עקיבא and רבי דוסא each convinced רבי יהושע that the בית דין's declaration is binding, and רבן גמליאל greeted him as 'my teacher and my student.' The גמרא explains רבן גמליאל's family tradition that the moon sometimes comes by a long path and sometimes by a short one, and רבי יוחנן finds a source for it in a פסוק. It adds stories about רבי חייא and the moon, and a ברייתא where רבן גמליאל used the exact length of the lunar month to stop a mistaken declaration. It then clarifies that רבי יהושע was the one who was upset, and brings רבי עקיבא's derivation from the triple 'אתם': the court's declaration stands even if made by mistake, on purpose, or because it was misled. Finally a ברייתא explains why the seventy זקנים are unnamed: so that no one belittles the judges of his own generation.

steps.title: End of the first testimony and רבי יוחנן בן נורי's objection
steps.stepSummary: The witnesses finish their claim: they saw the moon in the evening in the west. רבי יוחנן בן נורי declares them עדי שקר.
steps.simpleTranslation: "...and in the evening in the west." רבי יוחנן בן נורי said: They are false witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the משנה in the middle of a story. The witnesses said they saw the old moon in the morning in the east and the new moon that same evening in the west, and רבי יוחנן בן נורי says this cannot be true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the testimony ("we saw it in the morning in the east") is on the previous עמוד. The old moon and the new moon cannot both be seen on the same day, so to רבי יוחנן בן נורי the testimony contradicts itself. That makes them עדי שקר in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: in the evening
the west, where the new moon appears after sunset
false witnesses

steps.confusionAlert: This step starts in the middle of a sentence. The words "וערבית במערב" finish the witnesses' testimony from the previous עמוד. They are not a new statement.

phrases.english: and in the evening in the west.
phrases.notes: Finishes the witnesses' words. They had said: we saw it in the morning in the east.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said:
They are false witnesses.
phrases.notes: You cannot see the old moon and the new moon on the same day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי עֵדֵי שֶׁקֶר הֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's first story from the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי יוחנן בן נורי's view, witnesses who claim to see the old moon and the new moon on the same day are עדי שקר.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל accepts the witnesses anyway
steps.stepSummary: When the witnesses came to יבנה, רבן גמליאל accepted their testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they came to יבנה, רבן גמליאל accepted them.
steps.whatsHappening: Even though רבי יוחנן בן נורי called them liars, רבן גמליאל, the head of the בית דין in יבנה, accepted the testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל did not see the testimony as false. The גמרא (step 10) gives his reason: a family tradition that the moon sometimes comes by a long path and sometimes by a short one. The story shows that the head of the בית דין decides.

keyTerms.meaning: Yavneh, the town where the main בית דין sat
he accepted them, meaning he accepted their testimony
רבן גמליאל, the נשיא and head of the בית דין

phrases.english: When they came to Yavneh,
Rabban Gamliel accepted them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁבָּאוּ לְיַבְנֶה קִיבְּלָן רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the outcome of the first story, against רבי יוחנן בן נורי's objection.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל accepted the testimony despite the objection.

steps.title: A second case: seen on the 30th night, not seen on the next night
steps.stepSummary: Two witnesses saw the moon at its expected time, but no one saw it the next night. רבן גמליאל still accepted them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another time, two witnesses came and said: We saw it at its proper time. But on the next night, the night of the full month, it was not seen. And רבן גמליאל accepted them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a second story. Witnesses said they saw the new moon on the night of the 30th, but on the following night no one could see it. רבן גמליאל accepted them anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the new moon appears, it grows and should be even easier to see the next night. So when it was not seen the next night, the first sighting looks doubtful. Still, רבן גמליאל declared ראש חודש on the 30th day based on these witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: and another time
at its expected time, the night of the 30th
the night of the full month, the start of the 31st day

phrases.english: And another time, two came and said:
We saw it at its proper time,
phrases.notes: On the night of the 30th day.

phrases.english: but on the night of its full month, it was not seen,
phrases.notes: The next night, when a full 30-day month would end.

phrases.english: and Rabban Gamliel accepted them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד בָּאוּ שְׁנַיִם וְאָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second, separate story of the same type.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל declared ראש חודש on the 30th day even though the moon was not seen the following night.

steps.title: רבי דוסא בן הורכינס calls the second witnesses false
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא בן הורכינס says they are עדי שקר. He compares it to testifying that a woman gave birth while the next day she is clearly still pregnant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא בן הורכינס said: They are false witnesses. How can people testify that a woman gave birth, and the next day her belly is still out to her teeth?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסא בן הורכינס challenges רבן גמליאל's decision. He says this testimony is plainly disproven by what happened the next night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His comparison works like this. If a woman gave birth, she cannot look fully pregnant the next day. In the same way, if the moon was really seen on the 30th, it cannot be invisible on the 31st. So the next night's facts prove the witnesses wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: how can
they testify
her belly is between her teeth, meaning she is visibly very pregnant

phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa ben Horkinas said:
They are false witnesses.
How can they testify about a woman that she gave birth
and the next day her belly is between her teeth?
phrases.notes: A picture of something plainly disproven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי דּוֹסָא בֶּן הוֹרְכִּינָס עֵדֵי שֶׁקֶר הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבן גמליאל's acceptance of the second witnesses.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's acceptance of the witnesses in the second case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the moon was really seen on the 30th, it must be visible on the 31st. Since it was not seen, the next night proves the testimony false.

steps.title: רבי יהושע agrees with Rabbi Dosa
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע tells רבי דוסא that he finds his argument convincing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: I see your words.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע publicly sides with רבי דוסא against רבן גמליאל. This sets up the conflict in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By agreeing, רבי יהושע holds that ראש חודש should have been one day later. That would also push all the holidays of the month, including יום הכפורים, one day later.

keyTerms.meaning: I see your words, meaning I agree with your reasoning

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
I see your words.
phrases.notes: I agree with your argument.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ רוֹאֶה אֲנִי אֶת דְּבָרֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי דוסא's challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע agrees that the witnesses should not have been accepted.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's decree: come on your יום הכפורים with staff and money
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל orders רבי יהושע to come to him with his staff and money on the day רבי יהושע counts as יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל sent to him: I decree on you that you come to me with your staff and your money on the day that is יום הכפורים according to your count.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל responds to רבי יהושע with his authority as head of the בית דין. He orders רבי יהושע to act in public as if רבי יהושע's יום הכפורים is a regular weekday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying a staff and money is forbidden on יום הכפורים. By רבן גמליאל's count, that day is the 11th of תשרי, an ordinary day. The order forces רבי יהושע to show in public that the בית דין's calendar is the one that counts.

keyTerms.meaning: he sent a message to him
I decree upon you
your staff and your money, things one may not carry on יום הכפורים
your calculation, your count of the calendar

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the בית דין's decision about the calendar must be followed by everyone, even a great חכם who disagrees.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel sent to him:
I decree upon you that you come to me
with your staff and with your money
on the Yom Kippur that falls according to your calculation.
phrases.notes: By רבן גמליאל's count, this day is the 11th of תשרי.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁלַח לוֹ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל גּוֹזְרַנִי עָלֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבן גמליאל responds to רבי יהושע's disagreement by using his authority.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone must follow the בית דין's calendar, even on what one personally thinks is יום הכפורים.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא comforts רבי יהושע with a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא finds רבי יהושע upset and proves from a פסוק that whatever רבן גמליאל declared is valid, even if it was not at the right time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא went and found him distressed. He said to him: I can learn that everything רבן גמליאל did is valid, as it says: "These are the מועדים of ה׳, holy gatherings, which you shall proclaim." Whether at their time or not at their time, I have no מועדים other than these.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע is upset because he would have to treat what he believes is יום הכפורים like a weekday. רבי עקיבא proves from the תורה that the בית דין's declaration decides the date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says "אשר תקראו אתם", "which YOU shall proclaim." The מועדים are whatever the בית דין proclaims. So even if רבן גמליאל was mistaken about the moon, his declaration still sets יום הכפורים, and רבי יהושע's personal count does not.

keyTerms.meaning: distressed, upset
done, meaning valid and binding
which you shall proclaim them, the key words in the פסוק
not at their proper time

steps.whatToRemember: The calendar follows the בית דין's declaration ("אשר תקראו אתם"), even if that declaration was a mistake. Whatever רבן גמליאל declared is binding.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא is not saying רבן גמליאל was right about the moon. He is saying that even if the declaration was "not at its time," it still counts.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that the בית דין's קידוש החודש decides the dates of the holidays, even if the declaration was a mistake.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva went and found him distressed.
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: He said to him: I can learn

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכׇּל מַה שֶּׁעָשָׂה רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל עָשׂוּי,
phrases.english: that everything Rabban Gamliel did is valid,
as it is said: "These are the appointed times of ה׳,
holy gatherings, which you shall proclaim"
phrases.notes: ויקרא כ״ג:ד

phrases.english: whether at their time or not at their time,
I have no appointed times other than these.
phrases.notes: Only the ones the בית דין proclaimed.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ לִי לִלְמוֹד שֶׁכׇּל מַה שֶּׁעָשָׂה רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל עָשׂוּי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבן גמליאל's authority and resolves רבי יהושע's distress.
steps.raayaObject: Whatever the בית דין declares about the calendar is binding, even if it was not at the right time.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא כ״ג:ד: "אלה מועדי ה׳ מקראי קדש אשר תקראו אתם"

steps.title: רבי דוסא proves that every official court has the authority of משה's court
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע visits רבי דוסא בן הורכינס. רבי דוסא tells him that if we question רבן גמליאל's court, we would have to question every court since משה. He proves this from the fact that the names of the seventy elders are never given.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע came to רבי דוסא בן הורכינס. רבי דוסא said to him: 'If we start to question the rulings of רבן גמליאל's court, then we have to question every single court that has existed from משה's time until today. The פסוק says: "Then משה went up, and אהרן, נדב and אביהוא, and seventy of the elders of Israel." Why doesn't the תורה tell us the names of these elders? To teach that any group of three judges serving as an official בית דין over Israel has the same standing as משה's court.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע now goes to רבי דוסא, the same רבי דוסא who first called the witnesses liars. Even רבי דוסא tells him that he must accept רבן גמליאל's ruling, and he backs this up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי דוסא does not take back his opinion that the witnesses were wrong. He makes a different point: the authority of a בית דין does not depend on how great its judges are. The תורה leaves the seventy elders unnamed to show that what counts is being the official court, not being famous.

keyTerms.meaning: To question or re-examine a ruling after it was given
A Jewish court
Elders; here, the seventy elders who went up with משה
Their names were not spelled out
Every group of three judges

steps.confusionAlert: רבי דוסא does not say the witnesses were right. He still disagrees with רבן גמליאל on the facts. His point is only that the court's official ruling is binding anyway.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a core principle: the ruling of the current official בית דין binds everyone, even if earlier courts seemed greater. This idea runs through all of halachic authority.

phrases.aramaic: בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל רַבִּי דּוֹסָא בֶּן הוֹרְכִּינָס,
phrases.english: He (רבי יהושע) came to Rabbi Dosa ben Horkinas,
he (רבי דוסא) said to him:
If we come to question

phrases.aramaic: אַחַר בֵּית דִּינוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: the rulings of Rabban Gamliel's court,
we must also question

phrases.aramaic: אַחַר כׇּל בֵּית דִּין וּבֵית דִּין
phrases.english: the rulings of each and every court
that has stood from the days of Moses until now.
As it says: "Then Moses and Aaron went up,
Nadav and Avihu,
and seventy of the elders of Israel" (Shemos 24:9),
and why were they not spelled out,
the names of the elders?
phrases.notes: This is a rhetorical question that sets up the lesson.

phrases.english: Rather, to teach that every group of three
who stood as a court over Israel —

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הוּא כְּבֵית דִּינוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה.
phrases.english: it is like the court of Moses.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיַּעַל מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן נָדָב וַאֲבִיהוּא וְשִׁבְעִים מִזִּקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי עקיבא's proof in step 7, רבי יהושע gets a second confirmation, this time from רבי דוסא, the one who originally challenged the witnesses.
steps.raayaObject: Every official בית דין, even one less famous than משה's, has binding authority like משה's court.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות כ״ד:ט׳. The seventy זקנים who went up with משה are left unnamed, which shows that authority comes from the court's official role.

steps.title: רבי יהושע submits and רבן גמליאל greets him as teacher and student
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע takes his staff and money and goes to יבנה on the day that, by his own calculation, was יום הכפורים. רבן גמליאל stands, kisses him on the head, and calls him 'my teacher and my student.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע took his staff and his money in his hand. He went to יבנה, to רבן גמליאל, on the day that by his own calculation was יום הכפורים. רבן גמליאל stood up, kissed him on his head, and said: 'Come in peace, my teacher and my student! My teacher in wisdom, and my student because you accepted my words.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the story. רבי יהושע carries out רבן גמליאל's order, and רבן גמליאל honors him warmly for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying a staff and money is forbidden on יום הכפורים. By doing this on his own calculated date, רבי יהושע showed that he fully accepted the court's calendar over his own opinion. רבן גמליאל's greeting honors both sides: רבי יהושע was the greater scholar, but he still submitted to the court's authority.

keyTerms.meaning: His staff and his money
Yavne, the seat of רבן גמליאל's בית דין
According to his own calculation
My teacher and my student
Because you accepted my words

steps.whatToRemember: The story ends in peace. The greater scholar submits to the court in charge, and the head of the court honors him for his wisdom and his humility.

phrases.english: He took his staff and his money in his hand,
and went to Yavne, to Rabban Gamliel,
on the day that Yom Kippur fell
according to his own calculation.

phrases.aramaic: עָמַד רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וּנְשָׁקוֹ עַל רֹאשׁוֹ,
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel stood up and kissed him on his head,
he said to him: Come in peace,
my teacher and my student!
My teacher — in wisdom,
and my student — because you accepted my words.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָטַל מַקְלוֹ וּמְעוֹתָיו בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Persuaded by רבי עקיבא and רבי דוסא, רבי יהושע now does exactly what רבן גמליאל ordered in step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The court's calendar ruling stands. רבי יהושע fully accepts it, and the conflict ends with mutual respect.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's family tradition that the moon's path can be long or short
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא. רבן גמליאל tells the חכמים that he has a tradition from his grandfather's house: sometimes the moon comes by a long path and sometimes by a short one.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A ברייתא teaches that רבן גמליאל said to the חכמים: 'This is what I received from my grandfather's house: sometimes the moon comes by a long path, and sometimes it comes by a short path.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is over and the גמרא begins. It explains why רבן גמליאל accepted witnesses whom others called עדי שקר. Most directly, it answers רבי יוחנן בן נורי's objection to the first case: the old moon seen in the morning and the new moon that same evening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי (step 1) held that the old moon and the new moon cannot both be seen on the same day, so the witnesses must be lying. רבן גמליאל answers that the moon's monthly timing is not fixed: sometimes it comes by a short path and reappears very quickly. So the witnesses' report is possible. The same idea also helps explain his acceptance in the second case (steps 3–4).

keyTerms.meaning: The גמרא section, which discusses the משנה
It was taught in a ברייתא
I have received as a tradition
From the house of my father's father (my grandfather)
By a long path / by a short path

steps.confusionAlert: 'Long' and 'short' describe the moon's monthly cycle, meaning how long it takes before it reappears. They do not describe the moon's size.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught in a baraita,
Rabban Gamliel said to the Sages:
This is what I received from the house of my father's father —
sometimes it (the moon) comes by a long path
and sometimes it comes by a short path.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר לָהֶם רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לַחֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The story is finished, so the גמרא goes back to the factual disputes of the משנה (steps 1–4) and explains רבן גמליאל's reasoning for accepting the witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The length of the moon's monthly cycle varies. Sometimes the new moon reappears very quickly, even on the same day the old moon was last seen. So witnesses whose report seems impossible can still be truthful.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's source: the sun keeps a fixed schedule but the moon does not
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains the reason for the tradition of the house of the נשיא. The פסוק says 'the sun knows its setting,' which implies that the moon does not know its setting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: What is the reason of the house of רבי? It is written: 'He made the moon for the seasons; the sun knows its setting.' It is the sun that knows its setting. The moon does not know its setting.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a פסוק as the source for רבן גמליאל's family tradition that the moon's timing changes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says only about the sun that it 'knows its setting,' meaning it keeps a fixed, predictable schedule. Since the פסוק does not say this about the moon, it implies the moon's schedule is not fixed. That backs up the claim that the moon sometimes comes by a long path and sometimes by a short one.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Of the house of רבי, the family of the נשיא, to which רבן גמליאל belonged
Appointed times, seasons
Knows its setting, meaning it keeps a fixed schedule

steps.confusionAlert: 'דבי רבי' here refers to the house of the נשיא, רבן גמליאל's family line. It is not a new opinion from a different רבי. It is the same tradition from step 10.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the house of the נשיא, the moon's monthly cycle is not fixed the way the sun's is. So witnesses who report the new moon unusually soon after the old moon was seen can still be telling the truth. This also helps defend witnesses who saw it at its expected time even though it was not seen the next night.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
What is the reason of the house of Rabbi (the Nasi's family)?
As it is written: "He made the moon for seasons;
the sun knows its setting" (Tehillim 104:19) —
it is the sun that knows its setting,
the moon does not know its setting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as the source for the tradition רבן גמליאל cited in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The moon's cycle varies in length, unlike the sun's.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים ק״ד:י״ט, read precisely: only the sun is described as 'knowing its setting.'

steps.title: רבי חייא scolds the moon
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא saw the old moon still visible on the morning of the 29th. He threw a clod of earth at it and told it to hide, because the new moon had to be sanctified that night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא saw the moon standing in the sky on the morning of the twenty-ninth. He took a clod of earth and threw it at the moon, saying: 'Tonight we need to sanctify you, and you are still standing here?! Go cover yourself!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story showing how the moon's visibility can be unexpected. This fits the previous step, which said the moon 'does not know its setting.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the old moon can still be seen on the morning of the 29th, it seems unlikely that the new moon will be seen that night. רבי חייא was frustrated, because he wanted to sanctify ראש חודש on the 30th. The story illustrates that the moon does not follow a perfectly fixed, predictable path.

keyTerms.meaning: The moon (Aramaic)
Morning
A clod of earth
Tonight / this evening
Cover yourself / hide

steps.confusionAlert: רבי חייא is not actually controlling the moon. The story expresses his frustration that the old moon was still visible when the new moon was supposed to appear soon.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya saw the moon
that was standing in the sky on the morning of the twenty-ninth.
phrases.notes: This is the old, waning moon of the ending month.

phrases.english: He took a clod of earth and threw it at it,
he said: Tonight we need to sanctify you,
and you are still standing here?!
Go, cover yourself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא חַזְיֵיא לְסֵיהֲרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a story illustrating that the moon 'does not know its setting' (Step 11)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The moon's visibility is unpredictable; the old moon can still appear on the morning of the 29th.

steps.title: רבי sends רבי חייא to sanctify the month
steps.stepSummary: רבי told רבי חייא to go to עין טב and sanctify the month there. He was to send back the code phrase 'דוד מלך ישראל חי וקים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said to רבי חייא: 'Go to עין טב and sanctify the month, and send me a sign: "דוד, king of Israel, lives and endures."'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another short story about רבי חייא and the sanctifying of the month. This time it involves a secret signal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A code phrase was needed because, at that time, the ruling government had forbidden the sanctifying of the month. The phrase fits well because מלכות בית דוד is compared to the moon, which renews itself. 'David lives and endures' therefore hints that the moon was renewed and the month was sanctified.

keyTerms.meaning: A place name where the month was sanctified
The month (literally, the moon)
A sign / code signal
'David, king of Israel, lives and endures' (the code phrase)

steps.whyThisMatters: The source of the well-known phrase 'דוד מלך ישראל חי וקים,' which is still said today at קידוש לבנה.

phrases.english: Rebbi said to Rabbi Chiyya:
Go to Ein Tav and sanctify the month,
and send me a sign:
"David, king of Israel, lives and endures."
phrases.notes: מלכות בית דוד is compared to the moon (תהלים פ״ט), so this hints that the moon was renewed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about רבי חייא and sanctifying the month
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The month was sanctified by the court even in hard times, and a code phrase was used to report it.

steps.title: The court almost declares ראש חודש too early
steps.stepSummary: Through the clouds, people saw what looked like the moon on the 29th and wanted ראש חודש declared. רבן גמליאל stopped them with his family tradition that the lunar month is never shorter than 29 days, 12 hours, and 793 parts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Once the sky was covered with clouds, and the shape of a moon was seen on the 29th of the month. The people thought it was ראש חודש, and the court wanted to sanctify it. רבן גמליאל told them: 'This is what I received from my grandfather's house: the renewal of the moon is never less than 29 and a half days, two-thirds of an hour, and 73 parts.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing רבן גמליאל using his family's tradition about the moon in a real case. This connects to his tradition from Step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'moon' seen on the 29th could not really be the new moon, because the true lunar cycle is longer than 29 days. It was only an image created by the clouds. רבן גמליאל relied on his precise tradition about the cycle to override what people thought they saw.

keyTerms.meaning: The sky was bound up with clouds
The appearance (shape) of a moon
I have a tradition from my grandfather's house
The renewal of the moon (the lunar cycle)
Parts; an hour is divided into 1,080 parts

steps.confusionAlert: Two-thirds of an hour is 720 parts. Adding 73 parts gives 793 parts. So the month is 29 days, 12 hours, and 793 parts. This is the famous number used in the Jewish calendar.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Once the sky was covered with clouds,
and the shape of a moon was seen
on the twenty-ninth of the month.
The people thought to say it was Rosh Chodesh,
and the court sought to sanctify it.
Rabban Gamliel said to them:
This is what I received from my grandfather's house:
the renewal of the moon is not less
than twenty-nine and a half days
and two-thirds of an hour
and seventy-three parts.
phrases.notes: Out of 1,080 parts in an hour.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פַּעַם אַחַת נִתְקַשְּׁרוּ שָׁמַיִם בְּעָבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבן גמליאל's family tradition about the moon (Step 10) put into practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lunar month is never shorter than 29 days, 12 hours, and 793 parts, so a moon 'seen' before then is not the new moon.

steps.title: A public eulogy shows the month was not sanctified
steps.stepSummary: That same day, the mother of בן זזא died. רבן גמליאל gave her a large eulogy so that everyone would know the court had not declared ראש חודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: On that day the mother of בן זזא died, and רבן גמליאל gave her a great eulogy. This was not because she deserved such honor. It was so the people would know that the court had not sanctified the month.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the story. רבן גמליאל found a public way to show that the day was not ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eulogies are not given on ראש חודש. A large public eulogy was therefore a clear signal to everyone that the day was an ordinary weekday. This settled the confusion the clouds had caused.

keyTerms.meaning: A person whose mother died that day
A great eulogy
Worthy of this honor

steps.whatToRemember: רבן גמליאל relied on his precise tradition about the moon, not on a doubtful sighting. He then made sure the public knew no ראש חודש had been declared.

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם מֵתָה אִמּוֹ שֶׁל בֶּן זָזָא,
phrases.english: And on that day the mother of Ben Zaza died,
and Rabban Gamliel delivered a great eulogy for her.
Not because she was worthy of this,
but so that the people would know

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא קִידְּשׁוּ בֵּית דִּין אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: that the court had not sanctified the month.
phrases.notes: Eulogies are forbidden on ראש חודש.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם מֵתָה אִמּוֹ שֶׁל בֶּן זָזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברייתא's story by showing how the ruling was made public
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The court did not sanctify the month, and רבן גמליאל publicly signaled this by holding a eulogy.

steps.title: Who was the one who was upset?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'רבי עקיבא went and found him upset' and asks whether רבי עקיבא or רבי יהושע was the upset one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'רבי עקיבא went and found him upset, etc.' A question was asked: Who was upset? Was רבי עקיבא upset, or was רבי יהושע upset?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's story and points out that its wording is unclear. It is setting up a question that the next step will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Hebrew 'ומצאו מיצר' can be read two ways. It could mean that רבי עקיבא, being upset, went and found him. Or it could mean that רבי עקיבא found רבי יהושע, who was upset. The גמרא wants to know which reading is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: Distressed, upset
A question was raised before them
Etc. (the quote continues)

phrases.aramaic: הָלַךְ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וּמְצָאוֹ מֵיצֵר כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva went and found him distressed, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: A question was raised: Who was distressed?
Was Rabbi Akiva distressed,
or was Rabbi Yehoshua distressed?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מִי מֵיצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the moon and returns to the משנה's story of רבי עקיבא and רבי יהושע (Step 7)
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which person the משנה's word 'מיצר' refers to

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יהושע was upset
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא spells it out: רבי עקיבא found רבי יהושע upset. רבי יהושע said it would be better to be sick in bed for twelve months than to have this decree placed on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי עקיבא went and found רבי יהושע upset. He said to him: 'My teacher, why are you upset?' He answered: 'רבי עקיבא, it would be better for a person to fall sick in bed for twelve months than to have this decree issued against him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing a ברייתא that clearly names רבי יהושע as the upset one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's wording leaves no doubt: 'found רבי יהושע while he was upset.' רבי יהושע was deeply pained by רבן גמליאל's order to come with his staff and money on the day that, by his own calculation, was יום הכפורים. He felt that a year of illness would be easier than this decree.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a proof)
As it is taught in a ברייתא
Fall sick in bed
A decree

steps.whatToRemember: It was רבי יהושע who was upset, because he had to break the day he believed was יום הכפורים. רבי עקיבא was the one who came to comfort him.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: הָלַךְ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וּמְצָאוֹ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva went and found Rabbi Yehoshua
while he was distressed,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: [רַבִּי] מִפְּנֵי מָה אַתָּה מֵיצֵר?
phrases.english: he said to him: My teacher, why are you distressed?
He said to him: Rabbi Akiva,

phrases.aramaic: רָאוּי לוֹ שֶׁיִּפּוֹל לַמִּטָּה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: it is fitting for a person to fall sick in bed for twelve months,
rather than have this decree issued against him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע was the one who was upset, as the ברייתא states explicitly.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא asks permission to share a teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא politely asks רבי יהושע if he may repeat a lesson רבי יהושע once taught him. רבי יהושע says 'Speak.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: My teacher, allow me to say before you one thing that you taught me. He said to him: Speak.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא, who found רבי יהושע upset, asks permission to say something. This is a setup line that prepares the comforting proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא is careful to frame his words as רבי יהושע's own teaching, so he is not lecturing his רבי. Nothing new is proven yet. The step only opens the door for the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Allow me / give me permission
That you taught me
Speak / say it

phrases.english: He said to him: My teacher,
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא is speaking to רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: allow me to say before you
one thing that you taught me.
phrases.notes: He presents it as רבי יהושע's own teaching, out of respect.

phrases.english: He said to him: Speak.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: רַבִּי, תַּרְשֵׁינִי לוֹמַר לְפָנֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the scene from step 17, where רבי עקיבא found רבי יהושע upset.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. This is a narrative setup asking permission to share a teaching.

steps.title: The triple 'אֹתָם' teaches that the court's date stands even if mistaken
steps.stepSummary: The word 'אֹתָם' appears three times about proclaiming the holidays. Read as 'אַתֶּם' ('you'), it teaches that the court's declaration counts even if made by accident, on purpose, or because the court was fooled.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The תורה says 'them' ('אֹתָם'), 'them', 'them', three times. Read it as 'you' ('אַתֶּם'): 'You' even if by accident. 'You' even on purpose. 'You' even if you were misled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא proves from the פסוקים that whatever day the court declares as ראש חודש is binding. So רבי יהושע may follow רבן גמליאל's date without feeling he is violating the true יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אֹתָם' is written without a ו, so it can be read 'אַתֶּם', 'you'. That reading puts the power to fix the calendar in the court's hands. The three times cover three kinds of error: שוגג (an honest mistake), מזיד (deliberately), and מוטעה (fooled by false witnesses). In every case, the day the court declares is ראש חודש.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Them' as written, read as 'you'. It refers to the court that proclaims the holidays.
Acting by mistake, unknowingly
Acting on purpose
Misled, for example by false witnesses

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the court may change the calendar on a whim. It means that once the court has declared the day, the declaration binds everyone, even if it was wrong.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source for the rule that the court's קידוש החודש binds everyone, whatever the astronomy says. That is why רבי יהושע can submit to רבן גמליאל.

phrases.english: He said to him: Behold, it says
'them', 'them', 'them'
phrases.notes: ויקרא כ״ג:ב׳, ד׳, ל״ז, all about proclaiming the holidays.

phrases.english: three times.
'You', even if acting by mistake,
phrases.notes: 'אֹתָם' is read as 'אַתֶּם'.

phrases.english: 'You', even if acting on purpose,
'You', even if misled.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר ״אֹתָם״ ״אֹתָם״ ״אֹתָם״ שָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Delivers the teaching that רבי עקיבא asked permission to share.
steps.raayaObject: That the court's declaration of ראש חודש is binding, so רבי יהושע should accept רבן גמליאל's date.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The three appearances of 'אֹתָם' in ויקרא כ״ג, read as 'אַתֶּם'.

steps.title: רבי יהושע is comforted
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע tells רבי עקיבא, 'You have comforted me, you have comforted me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: In these words he said to him: עקיבא, you have comforted me, you have comforted me.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע accepts רבי עקיבא's proof. His distress from step 17 is resolved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works. Since the court's date binds everyone, treating the day he had calculated as יום הכפורים like a weekday is not a sin. The double 'נִחַמְתַּנִי' shows how deep his relief is.

keyTerms.meaning: You have comforted me
With these exact words

steps.whatToRemember: The court's ראש חודש declaration stands even if it was a mistake, deliberate, or based on false witnesses. Because of this, רבי יהושע could follow רבן גמליאל with a clear conscience.

phrases.english: In these words he said to him:
Akiva, you have comforted me, you have comforted me.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּלָּשׁוֹן הַזֶּה אָמַר לוֹ: עֲקִיבָא נִחַמְתַּנִי, נִחַמְתַּנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהושע's reaction to the proof in step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהושע is consoled. The court's declaration is binding, so following רבן גמליאל is correct.

steps.title: Why are the names of the seventy elders not recorded?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next scene, the visit to רבי דוסא בן הורכינס. It then brings a ברייתא that asks why the תורה does not name the זקנים who served with משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came to רבי דוסא בן הורכינס, and so on. The Rabbis taught: Why were the names of these elders not spelled out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה, where רבי דוסא argued that every court must be respected like משה's court. It brings a ברייתא question that leads into that idea, and sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי דוסא points out that the Torah never names the seventy זקנים, which shows that any court is like משה's court. The ברייתא now asks directly why those names are missing. It treats the missing names as deliberate.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא רבי יהושע visited next in the משנה
The Rabbis taught. This introduces a ברייתא.
Were spelled out, made explicit
The seventy elders who judged with משה

phrases.aramaic: בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל רַבִּי דּוֹסָא בֶּן הוֹרְכִּינָס כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: He came to Rabbi Dosa ben Horkinas, etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words to show which part it is now discussing.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Why were they not spelled out,
the names of these elders?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לָמָּה לֹא נִתְפָּרְשׁוּ שְׁמוֹתָם שֶׁל זְקֵנִים הַלָּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the רבי עקיבא scene to the next scene in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the Torah leaves out the names of the seventy זקנים.

steps.title: So no one can belittle the judges of his own generation
steps.stepSummary: The names were left out so that no one can say a current judge is not as great as משה and אהרן, נדב and אביהוא, or אלדד and מידד.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that a person should not say: Is so-and-so like משה and אהרן? Is so-and-so like נדב and אביהוא? Is so-and-so like אלדד and מידד?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. Because the other זקנים are unknown, no one can compare today's judges to them and say today's judges fall short.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every name were known, people could measure their own judges against famous figures and refuse to listen. Leaving the names out means any properly appointed court counts as a continuation of משה's court. This is exactly why רבי יהושע must accept רבן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: So-and-so, an unnamed person
אהרן's sons, who went up with the זקנים at סיני
Two of the זקנים who prophesied in the camp (במדבר י״א)

phrases.english: So that a person should not say:
Is so-and-so like Moses and Aaron?
phrases.notes: Asked as a scornful question: 'Is this judge really on their level?'

phrases.english: Is so-and-so like Nadav and Avihu?
Is so-and-so like Eldad and Medad?

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמַר אָדָם: פְּלוֹנִי כְּמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The names were left out so that no one would compare current judges to the great figures of משה's time and dismiss their authority.

steps.title: First פסוק: שמואל names משה and אהרן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a פסוק in which שמואל tells the people that ה׳ made משה and אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it says: 'And שמואל said to the people: It is ה׳ Who made משה and אהרן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds support from נ״ך. It first cites שמואל mentioning משה and אהרן, which sets up a comparison with the next פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its own, this פסוק only names משה and אהרן, the greatest leaders. Its point appears when it is paired with the next פסוק, which lists much lesser leaders in the same speech.

keyTerms.meaning: And it says. This introduces an additional פסוק.
The נביא and judge whose farewell speech is quoted (שמואל א׳ י״ב)

phrases.english: And it says: 'And Samuel said to the people:'
phrases.notes: שמואל א׳ י״ב:ו׳

phrases.aramaic: ה׳ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה אֶת מֹשֶׁה וְאֶת אַהֲרֹן״.
phrases.english: 'It is the Lord Who made Moses and Aaron.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹמֵר: ״וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל הָעָם ה׳ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה אֶת מֹשֶׁה וְאֶת אַהֲרֹן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a פסוק to support the idea of step 22 that every generation's leaders deserve respect.
steps.raayaObject: That leaders of every generation have authority equal to משה's court.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א׳ י״ב:ו׳, read together with י״ב:י״א.

steps.title: Second פסוק: lesser leaders listed in the same speech
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא cites the next part of שמואל's speech, which lists ירובעל, בדן, יפתח, and שמואל as leaders ה׳ sent.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it says: 'And ה׳ sent ירובעל and בדן and יפתח and שמואל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second פסוק from the same speech. It names leaders far less great than משה and אהרן, and sets up the lesson the גמרא will draw from the pairing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lesser judges are mentioned in the same speech as משה and אהרן, all as leaders sent by ה׳. This hints that a leader in his own generation carries the same authority as the greatest leaders did in theirs.

keyTerms.meaning: A nickname for one of the שופטים
Another nickname for one of the שופטים
A שופט from גלעד

phrases.english: And it says: 'And the Lord sent Jerubaal'
phrases.notes: שמואל א׳ י״ב:י״א

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת בְּדָן וְאֶת יִפְתָּח וְאֶת שְׁמוּאֵל״.
phrases.english: 'and Bedan and Jephthah and Samuel.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹמֵר: ״וַיִּשְׁלַח ה׳ אֶת יְרוּבַּעַל וְאֶת בְּדָן וְאֶת יִפְתָּח וְאֶת שְׁמוּאֵל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the pair of פסוקים begun in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: That lesser leaders are counted alongside משה and אהרן.

steps.title: Identifying ירובעל, בדן, and יפתח
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains the names. ירובעל is גדעון, because he fought against the בעל. בדן is שמשון, because he came from דן. יפתח is simply יפתח.
steps.simpleTranslation: ירובעל is גדעון. Why was he called ירובעל? Because he made a quarrel with the בעל. בדן is שמשון. Why was he called בדן? Because he came from דן. יפתח means just what it says.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pauses to explain who the nicknamed leaders are. This identifies the lesser figures it will compare to משה and אהרן in the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ירובעל' comes from 'ריב', a quarrel, with the בעל. גדעון destroyed the בעל's altar. 'בדן' means 'from דן', describing שמשון's tribe. יפתח needs no explanation because it is his real name.

keyTerms.meaning: The שופט nicknamed ירובעל
A quarrel, fight
The שופט from שבט דן, nicknamed בדן
As it sounds, its plain meaning

phrases.english: 'Jerubaal', this is Gideon,
and why was he called Jerubaal?
Because he made a quarrel with the Baal.
phrases.notes: See שופטים ו׳:ל״ב.

phrases.english: 'Bedan', this is Samson,
and why was he called Bedan?
Because he came from Dan.
Jephthah, as it sounds.
phrases.notes: No nickname; it is his actual name.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״יְרוּבַּעַל״ — זֶה גִּדְעוֹן, וְלָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ יְרוּבַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the names listed in the פסוק of step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ירובעל is גדעון, בדן is שמשון, and יפתח is יפתח himself.
